q: Which boxer, born Cassius Clay, lit the Olympic cauldron at the 1996 Atlanta Games?
note: His hands shook badly from Parkinson's disease as he held the torch, and the stadium fell silent.

q: Which basketball star played alongside Bugs Bunny in the 1996 film Space Jam?
note: He had briefly quit basketball to play minor league baseball two years before making the film.

q: Which Brazilian soccer legend was born Edson Arantes do Nascimento?
note: He never much liked the nickname, which a schoolfriend seems to have coined as a joke.

q: Which Jamaican sprinter won the Olympic 100 metres title in 2008, 2012 and 2016?
note: At six foot five he was considered far too tall to be a great sprinter, right up until he was one.

q: Which heavyweight boxer was nicknamed Iron Mike?
note: He kept racing pigeons as a boy in Brooklyn and still kept them at the height of his fame.

q: Which American swimmer won eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics?
note: One of the eight was won by a hundredth of a second, on a final lunge for the wall.

q: Which American sprinter won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics?
note: His victories embarrassed a Games staged as a showcase for Nazi racial theories.

q: Which Argentine footballer scored the Hand of God goal against England in 1986?
note: Four minutes after punching that one in, he ran half the length of the field to score a goal often called the greatest ever.

q: Which player broke Major League Baseball's colour barrier when he joined the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1947?
note: His number 42 is retired across every team in the sport, the only number to be so honoured.

q: Which baseball slugger was nicknamed the Bambino and the Sultan of Swat?
note: He began his career as a star pitcher for Boston before being sold to the Yankees and remade as a hitter.

q: Which Englishman ran the first mile in under four minutes, in 1954?
note: He was a medical student who trained in his lunch hours, and his record was beaten just 46 days later.

q: In the 1980 Miracle on Ice, the American ice hockey team beat which country?
note: It was not the final, and the young Americans still had to beat Finland two days later to take the gold.

q: Which Canadian ice hockey player was known as The Great One?
note: His father built him a backyard rink in Ontario so he could skate every evening through the winter.

q: Which American tennis player is remembered for yelling You cannot be serious at umpires?
note: The outburst came at Wimbledon in 1981, and he later used the line as the title of his autobiography.

q: Which golfer won the 1997 Masters by twelve strokes at the age of twenty-one?
note: He became the youngest man to win the tournament, and courses around the world were lengthened in response to him.

q: Which Romanian gymnast scored the first perfect ten in Olympic history, at Montreal in 1976?
note: The scoreboard could not display a ten, so her mark flashed up as 1.00 and the crowd had to be told what it meant.

q: Which tennis player beat Bobby Riggs in the 1973 Battle of the Sexes match?
note: She won in straight sets in front of a Houston crowd of over thirty thousand, and millions more on television.

q: Which president handed over the trophy at the 1995 Rugby World Cup final wearing a Springbok jersey?
note: The green jersey had been a symbol of apartheid, and his wearing it was the point of the gesture.

q: Which horse won the American Triple Crown in 1973, taking the Belmont Stakes by 31 lengths?
note: A post-mortem found his heart was more than twice the size of an average thoroughbred's.

q: Which British ski jumper became a crowd favourite at the 1988 Calgary Olympics despite finishing last?
note: He was a plasterer who funded himself, wore borrowed kit, and was so short-sighted his goggles fogged over on the way down.
